newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Defeated Mobutu troops cleared from Congo province.
newsitem.headline: Defeated Mobutu troops cleared from Congo province.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's troops have taken full control of ex-Zaire's Kasai Province following incursions by defeated former government soldiers, state television reported on Friday.
Local residents said remnants of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's army that lost civil war in May entered Kasai's Sankuru district last month, looting, raping and burning homes.
The inhabitants called for help from Kabila, who proclaimed himself president of the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo after his forces entered Kinshasa in mid-May.
"The Sankuru region has finally been liberated. The government has sent troops there," the television said.
It did not say when Kabila's forces went in or if they met any resistance. The fate of the former soldiers was not clear.
State television said some Sankuru inhabitants were returning to their homes after most left, notably from the towns of Lodja, Lomela and Lubefu.

Kabila's Alliance forces, backed by Rwanda, met little resistance from Mobutu's unpaid and highly indisciplined troops as they swept across the vast country. The armed campaign began in the two Kivu provinces bordering Rwanda.
Kabila entered Kinshasa after Mobutu fled. The former president is ailing with cancer in Morocco.
Ex-soldiers were ordered to assemble for re-training at a Kitona camp, 400 km (240 miles) south-west of Kinshasa, before they could be absorbed into a new national army.
Many have refused, describing the order as humiliating.
